summary: This continuation develops the integer-pole Delange theorem needed for nonnegative arithmetic counting sequences. It separates ordinary Laplace integration from Dirichlet-series summation, builds a polynomial regularizer and squared-sine smoothing, and proves the monotonicity step that recovers the leading asymptotic. The resulting counting interface retains the full boundary continuation hypotheses, the factorial constant and the positive-abscissa factor 1/a. Finite alterations and lower-pole dominated errors preserve that leading term. Wood’s arithmetic constructions remain with ArithmeticStatistics.

nodes.title: Convergent Laplace integral
nodes.statement: For a normed additive group E with a real normed-space structure and a complex scalar action, HasLaplace f s z μ asserts that t ↦ exp(−st) • f(t) is Bochner integrable for μ and has integral z. Here f:ℝ→E, s:ℂ and z:E; the measure defaults to Lebesgue measure restricted to (0,∞). The counting applications use E=ℂ and explicitly cast their real functions to ℂ. For Lebesgue integration (0,∞) and [0,∞) give the same convergence and value.
hypotheses: The core predicate requires NormedAddCommGroup E, NormedSpace ℝ E and SMul ℂ E. Additivity requires DistribSMul ℂ E; complex scaling and positive dilation use NormedSpace ℂ E with IsScalarTower ℝ ℂ E. Dilation is for the default Lebesgue measure, not for an arbitrary μ.
proofSteps: Use the native Bochner integral with convergence as part of the predicate. The carrier, optional measure and scalar-action conventions follow the HasLaplace interface of Mathlib PR #40582; its E=ℂ specialization is used throughout the Tauberian argument. At the pinned baseline this is new material; adopt the Mathlib interface when it becomes available.

Projection lemmas expose convergence and the integral value. Uniqueness, μ-almost-everywhere congruence, addition and complex scaling use the Bochner integral API. For default Lebesgue measure, a positive change of variable proves dilation. The singleton endpoint has measure zero.
acceptance: The constant-one function has transform 1/s on Re(s)>0; at s=0 it is not integrable.

sources.match: The argument uses ordinary Laplace integration of the counting function, rather than a Stieltjes transform. The predicate records exactly that convergence.

nodes.title: Boundary continuation and pole numerator
nodes.statement: PoleBoundary F a k A consists of: F analytic on Re(s)>a; a radius r>0 and g analytic on the ball about a such that g(a)=A and F(s)=g(s)/(s−a)^(k+1) on its intersection with Re(s)>a; and, for each real y≠0, a radius r_y>0 and an analytic g_y about a+iy agreeing with F on the corresponding right-half-plane intersection. k is natural. A≠0 makes the pole order exactly k+1; the main theorems require A>0. Values assigned to F on the boundary carry no meaning.
proofSteps: Express each extension using AnalyticOnNhd and an explicit agreement domain. A local holomorphic remainder is absorbed into the numerator.
Use uniqueness of analytic germs on the intersection to obtain unique leading coefficient and, when nonzero, pole order.

Multiplication by a regular function multiplies the leading coefficient. Division by the argument is valid for a>0 and changes A to A/a. Rescaling s ↦ as moves the line to Re(s)=1 and changes A to A/a^(k+1).
acceptance: Boundary values of F can be changed arbitrarily without changing PoleBoundary. Positivity belongs to the main theorem, not to the carrier.

sources.locator: §5.2.1 Theorem III, pp.235–238; standing hypotheses p.213
sources.match: The integer specialization needs holomorphic extensions at every other point of the line and an analytic numerator at the pole. A one-sided real limit does not supply these hypotheses.

api.name: PoleBoundary.congr

api.name: PoleBoundary.leading_unique
api.statement: For fixed F,a,k, two leading coefficients A,B coincide.

api.name: PoleBoundary.order_unique
api.statement: For fixed F,a and nonzero leading coefficients, two indices k,l coincide.

api.name: PoleBoundary.div_argument

api.name: PoleBoundary.rescale

api.name: PoleBoundary.mul_regular

nodes.title: Normalized squared-sinc kernel
nodes.statement: For real λ,v set K_λ(v)=squaredSinc λ v=(λ/π) sinc(λv)², using Mathlib Real.sinc(0)=1. Its analytic and probability assertions assume λ>0. Angular Fourier frequency y is used: K_λ(v)=(1/(2π))∫_(−2λ)^(2λ)(1−|y|/(2λ))exp(iyv)dy.
proofSteps: Use the existing sinc function, its continuity and bound near zero. Away from zero the square is bounded by a constant times v^(−2), giving integrability.

Compute mass by integration by parts on a finite positive interval, reducing to the pinned improper sine-integral limit; evenness gives the full integral. There is no use of a Lebesgue integral of unsquared sinc.
Integrate the triangular frequency weight explicitly, including v=0 by continuity. Scaling and integrability give vanishing tails outside every fixed neighbourhood as λ tends to infinity.
acceptance: The continuous value at zero and frequency endpoint 2λ are fixed; this is a kernel on ℝ, distinct from the finite-circle Fejér expression in the sieve roadmap.

sources.match: The proof uses the square of the sine quotient with compact triangular frequency support. Here it is normalized to mass one, so the smoothing limit is a coefficient rather than π times that coefficient.

api.name: squaredSinc_nonneg
api.statement: K_λ(v)≥0 for λ>0 and all real v.

api.name: squaredSinc_even
api.statement: K_λ(−v)=K_λ(v).

api.name: squaredSinc_continuous
api.statement: K_λ is continuous for every real λ.

api.name: squaredSinc_integrable

api.name: squaredSinc_mass
api.statement: For λ>0, ∫ℝ K_λ=1.

api.name: squaredSinc_fourier
api.statement: The angular-frequency triangular integral in the definition statement equals K_λ, as a complex-valued equality.

api.name: squaredSinc_tail
api.statement: For h>0, ∫_(|v|≥h)K_λ(v)dv tends to 0 as λ tends to infinity.

tests.name: squaredSinc_test_mass_two

uses.how: Its compact Fourier support allows use of locally L1 boundary values.
Positivity, mass one and tail decay turn monotonicity into two-sided bounds.

nodes.title: Polynomial Laplace regularization weight
nodes.statement: For k∈ℕ and t∈ℝ define w_k(t)=delangeWeight k t=t∫_0^1 exp(−ut)u^k/k! du. It is zero at t=0, positive for t>0, and satisfies w_k(t)t^k→1 as t→∞. Its definition is total; positivity and upper bounds are asserted only for t≥0.
proofSteps: Change variable x=ut. For t>0, w_k(t)t^k=(1/k!)∫_0^t exp(−x)x^k dx.

Use GammaIntegral_convergent after positive scaling, the real Gamma integral and Γ(k+1)=k! to obtain normalization and the bound ≤1. The integral on [0,1] depends continuously on t, by dominated convergence uniformly on each compact t interval.

The normalization and (t+h)^k/t^k→1 yield w_k(t+h)/w_k(t)→1 for every fixed real h. For a fixed H>0 this convergence is uniform over |h|≤H: both normalized weights approach 1 uniformly once t−H is large, and ((t+h)/t)^k approaches 1 uniformly. The first three indices follow by elementary integration.
acceptance: The weight is not identically t^(−k) near the origin; the vanishing at zero makes the ordinary integral regularizer precise.

sources.match: Specializing the source regularizer to integer powers gives this explicit Gamma-normalized weight. The cutoff 1 is a positive fixed cutoff; the argument and limit are independent of its particular positive value.

api.name: delangeWeight_continuous
api.statement: For every natural k, the total real function w_k is continuous on ℝ.

api.name: delangeWeight_nonneg
api.statement: w_k(t)≥0 for t≥0.

api.name: delangeWeight_pos
api.statement: w_k(t)>0 for t>0.

api.name: delangeWeight_normalization
api.statement: w_k(t)t^k→1 as t→∞.

api.name: delangeWeight_shift
api.statement: For each fixed h∈ℝ, w_k(t+h)/w_k(t)→1.

api.name: delangeWeight_bound
api.statement: For t≥0, w_k(t)t^k≤1.

tests.name: delangeWeight_test_double
tests.statement: t w_1(t)=1−(1+t)exp(−t) for every real t.

tests.name: delangeWeight_test_triple

uses.how: Multiplication by w_k corresponds to integrating the negative derivative of the transform against u^k/k!.
The shift law permits comparison of the weighted count at t and nearby arguments without assuming it monotone.
Continuity bounds w_k on compact intervals. Its normalized form also gives uniform shift ratios on every fixed bounded range of shifts.

nodes.title: Integer Gamma Laplace model
nodes.statement: For k∈ℕ, a∈ℝ and complex s with Re(s)>a, the function α(t)=exp(at)t^k has HasLaplace value k!/(s−a)^(k+1).
proofSteps: The norm is exp(−(Re(s)−a)t)t^k. Positive scaling of GammaIntegral_convergent proves its integrability; the real Gamma integral separately evaluates its norm integral.
Start with the pinned complex exponential integral at k=0; repeated integration by parts proves the formula for every integer k. Exponential decay removes each endpoint at infinity.
Thus β(t)=(A/k!)exp(at)t^k has transform A/(s−a)^(k+1), with no truncation error or choice of complex powers.
acceptance: For k=0 the transform is 1/(s−a); for k=1 it is 1/(s−a)².

sources.match: The Gamma model identifies the pole term with its ordinary Laplace inverse. Only positive integer pole orders are needed here.

nodes.title: Locally integrable regularized boundary
nodes.statement: Assume PoleBoundary F a k A. Set R(s)=F(s)−A/(s−a)^(k+1) on Re(s)>a and H(s)=−∫_0^1 R′(s+u)u^k/k! du. There is b:ℝ→ℂ such that, for every L>0, b is integrable on [−L,L] and ∫_(−L)^L |H(a+ε+iy)−b(y)|dy→0 as ε↓0. All derivative evaluations in this limit have ε>0.
hypotheses: PoleBoundary F a k A; k∈ℕ; no positivity or Laplace representation is needed for this analytic lemma.
proofSteps: Apply the existing Laurent decomposition to the local analytic numerator quotient, not to the arbitrary boundary values of F. Subtracting the leading term leaves poles of orders at most k and a holomorphic remainder.

Split u∈[0,1] into the part inside the pole ball and its compact regular complement. A remaining pole of order j≤k contributes a derivative bounded by a constant times |u+ε+iy|^(−j−1). Since |u+ε+iy|≥(u+|y|)/√2 for ε,u≥0, its u^k-weighted integral is bounded, for 0<|y| small and all sufficiently small ε>0, by C(1+|log|y||). For k=0 the remainder is regular. This majorant is locally integrable; the single y=0 is ignored almost everywhere.
Away from zero, boundary germs and compactness of the u interval give ordinary convergence and a uniform bound. Patch a finite cover of each y interval.
Define b by the limit away from zero, assigning any finite value at zero. Apply dominated convergence to the norm of the difference; the logarithmic majorant gives L1 convergence.
acceptance: A lower pole of order k produces at most logarithmic boundary growth after regularization, rather than an unintegrable power.

sources.match: This is the holomorphic-boundary specialization of the regularized transform step. It replaces the source broader boundary-limit machinery by compact L1 convergence under the stronger hypotheses used in this roadmap.

nodes.title: Higher-pole smoothed counting limit
nodes.statement: Let a>0, k∈ℕ and A∈ℝ. Let α be nonnegative and nondecreasing on [0,∞), HasLaplace (t ↦ (α(t):ℂ)) s (F(s)) for all Re(s)>a, and PoleBoundary F a k A. For every λ>0 and T∈ℝ the integral ∫_0^∞ w_k(t)exp(−at)α(t)K_λ(t−T)dt is absolutely integrable, and as T→∞ it tends to A/k!.
hypotheses: a>0; α(t)≥0 for t≥0; MonotoneOn α [0,∞); convergence at every s with Re(s)>a; full PoleBoundary, not only a local pole.
proofSteps: Subtract β=(A/k!)exp(at)t^k. For a fixed s with Re(s)>a choose a<σ₀<σ₁<Re(s) and a neighbourhood on which Re(z)≥σ₁. Convergence at the real point σ₀ gives the integrable norm majorant exp(−σ₀t)|α(t)−β(t)|; t exp(−(σ₁−σ₀)t) is bounded. Apply hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le with restricted half-line measure to differentiate the transform R. Fubini, with u∈[0,1], then gives H(s)=∫_0^∞ exp(−st)w_k(t)(α(t)−β(t))dt.
Insert the triangular Fourier formula for K_λ in the ε-damped integral. The u,t,y interchanges are justified at ε>0 by absolute convergence and compact frequency support.

Use regularizedBoundaryL1 to pass ε↓0 on the frequency side. The resulting compactly supported L1 Fourier product tends to zero as T→∞ by Real.tendsto_integral_exp_smul_cocompact, after converting angular frequency e^(−iyT) to Mathlib’s e^(−2πiyv) using v=T/(2π). On the counting side positivity gives undamped integrability by Fatou and the finite damped limit; the Gamma model term is integrable because w_k(t)t^k≤1. Dominated convergence removes ε using the undamped nonnegative product as majorant. This proves the undamped identity before taking its T limit.
For the model, w_k(t)t^k is bounded by 1 and tends to 1. Translation, dominated convergence and ∫K_λ=1 give model limit A/k!, so the count has that same smoothed limit.
acceptance: No bound α(t)=O(exp(at)t^k) is assumed: that bound is obtained in the next monotonicity step.

sources.match: The squared-sine convolution extracts the leading coefficient from the regularized transform. Positivity justifies passing from damped integrals to their undamped counterparts.

nodes.title: Monotone removal of squared-sine smoothing
nodes.statement: Let a>0, C≥0 and k∈ℕ. Suppose α is nonnegative and nondecreasing on [0,∞). Assume that for every λ>0 the smoothed integral in HP.2 is integrable for every T and tends to C as T→∞. Then α(t)/(exp(at)t^k)→C as t→∞.
hypotheses: No transform or boundary hypothesis is used here; all positive λ are required, along with their actual convolution limits and integrability.
proofSteps: Write J(t)=w_k(t)exp(−at)α(t) for t≥0. Fix h>0 and a positive λ whose kernel has positive mass on [−h/2,h/2]. In the convolution centred at T+h/2, restrict t to [T,T+h]. Monotonicity gives α(t)≥α(T); the uniform shift ratio from w_k(t)t^k→1 and exp(−ah) give a positive multiple of J(T) as a lower bound. The smoothed limit therefore bounds J eventually. Monotonicity bounds α on compact intervals and continuity bounds w_k there, so J has a global bound M on [0,∞).

For the upper bound on J(T), use the same right interval and centre T+h/2. For the lower bound, centre the convolution at T−h/2, restrict t to [T−h,T], and use α(t)≤α(T), the uniform weight ratio and exp(ah); the omitted contribution is at most M times the kernel mass outside [−h/2,h/2].

Let T→∞ at fixed λ,h. Then let λ→∞ for fixed h>0: the interval mass tends to one and the tail mass to zero by squaredSinc_tail. Finally let h↓0; the exponential comparison factors approach one, and limsup and liminf of J are both C.
Use w_k(t)t^k→1 to replace J(t) by α(t)/(exp(at)t^k). This also proves the case C=0.
acceptance: The weighted function J itself need not be monotone. A limit for one fixed bandwidth is insufficient for this statement.

sources.match: The Tauberian step uses the nondecreasing counting function and the shift behaviour of the regularizer. It derives the necessary bound instead of taking the intended asymptotic as a premise.

nodes.title: Delange integer-pole Laplace theorem
nodes.statement: Let a>0, A>0 and m=k+1 with k∈ℕ. If α:[0,∞)→[0,∞) is nondecreasing, its ordinary Laplace integral is F(s) for Re(s)>a, and PoleBoundary F a k A holds, then α(t)/(exp(at)t^k)→A/k!. Equivalently α(t)∼(A/k!)exp(at)t^k.
hypotheses: Nonnegative finite real α and MonotoneOn on [0,∞); local integrability follows from monotonicity. Convergence and boundary assertions are the separate predicates of HP.0.
proofSteps: Apply delangeSmoothedLimit for every λ>0.
A/k!>0 since A>0. Apply monotoneUnsmoothing with this C.
Use m=k+1 to identify k!=(m−1)!; the denominator is eventually positive.
acceptance: For m=1 the result reduces to the simple-pole exponential asymptotic under holomorphic boundary extensions. For m=2 it has coefficient A and one power of t.

sources.locator: §5.2.1 Theorem III, pp.235–238; standing hypotheses p.213
sources.match: This is the positive integer exponent specialization of Theorem III, proved through the recorded smoothing and monotonicity chain.

nodes.title: Inclusive logarithmic summatory Laplace bridge
nodes.statement: For c:ℕ→ℝ with c_n≥0, let S_c(X)=TauCeti.summatory id ĉ X, where ĉ(0)=0 and ĉ(n)=c_n for n>0. Put α(t)=S_c(exp t) for t≥0. If Re(s)>0 and LSeriesHasSum (c cast to ℂ) s (F(s)), then HasLaplace (t ↦ (α(t):ℂ)) s (F(s)/s). Moreover α is nonnegative and nondecreasing, and α(0)=c_1.
hypotheses: Nonnegative coefficients; actual LSeriesHasSum at s; Re(s)>0, even when the series happens to converge at a nonpositive real part.
proofSteps: Use the existing Northcott summatory function; no second finite-cutoff carrier is introduced. Its sum is inclusive, so n=1 is present at t=0.
Write α(t)=Σ_(n≥1)c_n 1_(log n≤t). The n=0 term of LSeries is zero and must not be inserted as mass.
The sum of integrals of norms is Σ_(n≥1)c_n n^(−Re(s))/Re(s), finite by absolute convergence. Interchange sum and integral using integral_tsum.
Integrate each tail exp(−st) from log n to infinity to obtain c_n n^(−s)/s. Sum using LSeriesHasSum. Nonnegativity and monotonicity are existing summatory API composed with exp.
acceptance: logSummatory_test_initial: S_c(exp 0)=c_1. logSummatory_test_unit_mass: the sole coefficient c_1=1 gives transform 1/s. logSummatory_test_endpoint: S_c(exp(log 2))=c_1+c_2. These are explicit suggested-file examples.

sources.locator: Standing hypotheses p.213; §5.2.1 Theorem III, pp.235–238
sources.match: The source theorem is an ordinary Laplace theorem. This direct absolute-convergence adapter establishes the Dirichlet-series interface, with division by s and the inclusive n=1 mass.
The arithmetic counting application motivates this independently derived inclusive Dirichlet-to-Laplace adapter.

nodes.title: Delange higher-pole Dirichlet counting theorem
nodes.statement: Let c_n≥0 and A>0. Assume F(s) is the LSeriesHasSum value of c for every Re(s)>1 and PoleBoundary F 1 k A holds. Then S_c(X)/(X(log X)^k)→A/k! as X→∞, where S_c excludes n=0 and includes every 1≤n≤X.
hypotheses: k∈ℕ, so m=k+1≥1; positive leading coefficient; genuine local analytic extensions along the entire line.
proofSteps: The bridge gives α(t)=S_c(exp t) with transform F(s)/s.
PoleBoundary.div_argument at a=1 preserves the leading coefficient A. Apply delangeLaplace.
Substitute t=log X for X>1 and use exp(log X)=X and log X→∞. This gives the inclusive real-cutoff conclusion.
acceptance: c_n=1 for n>0 gives S(X)/X→1; m=2 gives the divisor-counting denominator X log X.

sources.match: The Laplace theorem and explicit division-by-s adapter yield the higher-pole partial sum asymptotic required by Wood’s counting application.
Wood uses higher-order pole counting; the generic export retains explicit full boundary continuation supplied by the arithmetic consumer.

nodes.title: Positive-abscissa counting and scaling
nodes.statement: For a>0, A>0, k∈ℕ and c_n≥0, suppose F(s) is the LSeriesHasSum value for Re(s)>a and PoleBoundary F a k A holds. Then S_c(X)/(X^a(log X)^k)→A/(a k!). Real powers use Mathlib Real.rpow, and X>1 is automatic eventually.
hypotheses: a>0 is essential to this adapter and constant; no a=0 logarithmic-counting theorem is asserted.
proofSteps: Use the same logarithmic summatory bridge. PoleBoundary.div_argument changes the leading coefficient to A/a at the original line.
Apply delangeLaplace and substitute t=log X, using exp(a log X)=X^a.
For an independent normalization check, rescale the transformed variable s↦as: the leading coefficient becomes A/a^(k+1); the time dilation contributes a^k. Their product is A/a.
acceptance: At a=1 this agrees with delangeDirichlet. counting_test_abscissa_two: coefficients c_n=n give S_c(X)/X²→1/2, detecting a missing 1/a at the simple pole of ζ(s−1).

sources.locator: §5.2.1 Theorem III, pp.235–238; standing hypotheses p.213
sources.match: The source allows any positive abscissa. The factor 1/a comes from the ordinary Laplace transform of the logarithmic counting function.

nodes.title: Finite-change invariance of counting asymptotics
nodes.statement: For real sequences c,d agreeing outside a finite set, a>0 and k∈ℕ, if S_c(X)/(X^a(log X)^k)→C, then S_d(X)/(X^a(log X)^k)→C. The conclusion permits signed coefficients and does not require a series or boundary theorem.
hypotheses: Finite disagreement; a>0; k natural; a known asymptotic for c.
proofSteps: Apply the existing eventually_summatory_sub_eq to the zero-suppressed weights. Their difference is eventually the finite constant sum of coefficient changes.
X^a(log X)^k→∞ when a>0, so this fixed difference divided by the denominator tends to zero.
Transfer the limit by addition. A mass at n=1 is a constant contribution and is covered by this theorem.
acceptance: Inserting seven at n=1 into the divisor sequence leaves the X log X leading coefficient equal to one.

sources.match: Finite alterations change a summatory function by a bounded amount. The generic export states this elementary consequence using the existing finite-change summatory API.
Adding a constant to the counting function does not affect its leading asymptotic at a positive abscissa.

nodes.title: Lower-pole dominated signed perturbation
nodes.statement: Let a>0, B>0 and l<k be natural indices. Let b_n≥0 have a convergent Dirichlet series G on Re(s)>a and PoleBoundary G a l B. Suppose |d_n−c_n|≤b_n for every n and S_c(X)/(X^a(log X)^k)→C. Then S_d(X)/(X^a(log X)^k)→C. Thus a signed change dominated by a sequence of pole order l+1<k+1 is negligible at the higher counting scale.
hypotheses: The majorant b has its own convergence and full boundary hypotheses. A local pole of a formal perturbation alone is insufficient; c,d need not be nonnegative.
proofSteps: Apply the positive-abscissa theorem to b to get S_b(X)=O(X^a(log X)^l).
Use the finite sum triangle inequality and the coefficient bound to obtain |S_d(X)−S_c(X)|≤S_b(X).
Divide by the higher scale and use (log X)^(l−k)→0. Transfer the limit by the squeeze theorem.
acceptance: The strict inequality l<k rules out removing a same-order pole without changing the leading coefficient.

sources.locator: Wood §7 p.417; lower-rank removal after the Tauberian asymptotic
sources.match: Wood removes counts of smaller-rank images by bounding them by a lower-order counting sequence. This export provides the generic analytic estimate; the arithmetic majorant and its positivity stay in ArithmeticStatistics ST.3.

nodes.title: Divisor coefficients of the square of zeta
nodes.statement: For Re(s)>1, the nonnegative coefficient d(n)=#(Nat.divisors n) has LSeriesHasSum value ζ(s)². This F satisfies PoleBoundary F 1 1 1. Consequently Σ_(1≤n≤X)d(n)/(X log X)→1. The sequence has d(0)=0 by the existing divisor convention.
hypotheses: Use the analytic continuation riemannZeta, identified with its Dirichlet series only on Re(s)>1.
proofSteps: Use the existing arithmetic-function convolution identity ζ_arith*ζ_arith=σ_0 and sigma_zero_apply to identify d. LSeriesHasSum.convolution and the convergent zeta series give its transform.

analyticOn_riemannZeta supplies the away germs. The pinned residue limit and analyticity on a punctured ball imply a removable holomorphic extension of (s−1)ζ(s) with value 1. Its square gives the numerator with value 1 for an exact double pole.
Apply delangeDirichlet at k=1,A=1. Check d(4)=3, and apply finiteChange_asymptotic to the inserted n=1 mass.
The constant-one acceptance example uses the same residue germ at k=0; its conclusion also agrees with the elementary floor count.
acceptance: counting_test_ones: S_1(X)/X→1, with the n=0 coefficient suppressed. counting_test_divisors_four: d(4)=3. counting_test_insert_one: replacing d by d+7·1_(n=1) keeps the limit one.

sources.match: The simple and double zeta poles provide elementary checks of the integer-pole counting formula and factorial normalization. The arithmetic identities and continuation are imported from Mathlib.

nodes.title: Local-pole hypothesis rejection
nodes.statement: Let c_n=n if n=2^j for some j∈ℕ, and c_n=0 otherwise. For Re(s)>1 its convergent Dirichlet series is F(s)=1/(1−exp((1−s)log 2)). It has a local analytic numerator F(s)=g(s)/(s−1), g(1)=1/log 2. But PoleBoundary F 1 0 (1/log 2) is false, and S_c(X)/X does not tend to 1/log 2. In fact S_c(2^j)/2^j→2 and S_c(3·2^j)/(3·2^j)→4/3 as the natural index j→∞.
hypotheses: This is a rejection test for omitting the away-boundary field; its coefficients are nonnegative. The local numerator is explicitly required, not merely a real residue limit.
proofSteps: Reindex the absolutely convergent series by n=2^j, giving the geometric sum with ratio 2^(1−s). The denominator has a simple zero at 1 with derivative log 2, so the local numerator has the stated value.
At 1+2πi/log 2 the denominator vanishes again, and the singularity is a genuine pole. No holomorphic boundary extension there can agree on the open half-plane.
Compute S_c(2^j)=2^(j+1)−1 and S_c(3·2^j)=2^(j+2)−1. Dividing by the respective cutoffs gives limits 2 and 4/3 as j→∞.
Distinct subsequential limits exclude any global counting limit and in particular the proposed residue constant. This directly tests the theorem’s full boundary hypothesis.
acceptance: The counterexample passes nonnegativity, right-half-plane convergence and the exact local pole test, and fails only the full boundary requirement.

sources.locator: §5.3, p.242; contrast with Theorem III, pp.235–236
sources.match: Delange explains why information at the real singularity alone has weaker consequences. The dyadic geometric series is an independently computed witness of the necessary distinction, not an example attributed to the source.

ownershipNotes: Current TauCetiRoadmap main at 81207c7f16d5abf770f13a7d2bdcdb465c030787 and current Tau Ceti sources were read-only audit inputs. The parent README and Suggested.lean and Chebotarev README were read; the current later-added roadmaps have no competing higher-pole Tauberian export.

The existing completely-monotone Laplace transforms integrate measures or kernels at real nonnegative arguments. They do not provide a convergent complex-parameter ordinary transform for a growing counting function; HasLaplace uses the native Bochner integral directly. The finite-circle Fejér expression in SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns is not the normalized continuous squared-sinc kernel on ℝ. No shared object is duplicated.

The reviewed AnalyticNumberTheory AN.0 audit supplies LSeries and existing analytic summation tools, but no higher-pole Laplace or Dirichlet theorem. Current Tau Ceti WienerIkehara modules contain simple-pole Fourier identities, boundary limits and growth estimates, not this integer-pole regularization theorem.

The parent remains the first roadmap prerequisite. All mathematical node prerequisites resolve to exact pinned library declarations or nodes here, so no unbuilt supplier request is necessary. In particular generic finite-change summatory calculus and Laurent extraction are reused, not re-planned.

Independent review checked open Mathlib PR #40582 (https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/40582), head 90482cd37e85e423459de2ed103cea2f4d98cb20, and searched public Lean Zulip for Laplace/sinc design. The PR supplies HasLaplace with a normed target, complex scalar action, optional measure defaulting to volume.restrict (Ioi 0), congr_ae, const_smul and comp_mul_left. HP.0 follows that shape; it is not cited as an existing pinned declaration. No competing squared-sinc or higher-pole Tauberian design was found in these searches.
